> Awesome List of Fire Science Tools

## :material-robot: AI & Productivity Tools
URL: https://tyson-swetnam.github.io/awesome-fire-science/ai-tools.md

# :material-robot: AI & Productivity Tools

AI assistants and productivity tools can enhance research workflows, automate repetitive tasks, and accelerate data analysis. This page covers general-purpose AI tools, productivity software, and specialized geospatial AI models relevant to wildland fire science.

??? Tip "Important: Privacy & Security"
    Always check your agency or institution's IT policy before using AI tools with work data. Do not upload sensitive, proprietary, or confidential information to public AI services. Verify all AI-generated outputs for accuracy and do not rely on them without validation.

## :fontawesome-brands-openai: Generative AI Assistants

General-purpose large language models (LLMs) that can assist with code generation, data analysis, writing, and research tasks.

[:fontawesome-brands-openai: ChatGPT](https://chat.openai.com){target=_blank} - OpenAI's conversational AI with advanced reasoning capabilities, code generation, and creative writing. 🆓 Free tier available, 💰 $20/mo Plus with GPT-4 and extended capabilities.

[:simple-anthropic: Claude](https://claude.ai){target=_blank} - Anthropic's AI assistant with 200k token context window, excellent for long document analysis, research synthesis, and technical writing.

[:simple-google: Google Gemini](https://gemini.google.com){target=_blank} - Google's multimodal AI with deep integration into Google Workspace, supporting text, image, and data analysis.

[:material-microsoft: Microsoft Copilot](https://copilot.microsoft.com){target=_blank} - Microsoft's AI assistant integrated into Windows, Edge browser, and Office 365 applications.

[:material-magnify: Perplexity](https://www.perplexity.ai){target=_blank} - AI-powered search engine that provides sourced answers with citations, useful for research and fact-checking.

### Fire Science-Specific AI Applications

As AI tools continue to evolve, watch for specialized applications in wildland fire science. Current examples include:

[:material-brain: Allen AI Wildlands](https://allenai.org/wildlands){target=_blank} - AI research initiative focused on wildfire prediction, detection, and management using machine learning.

[:material-wifi: WIFIRE Firemap](https://wifire.ucsd.edu/firemap){target=_blank} - Near real-time fire mapping using AI and satellite imagery.

## :material-briefcase: Productivity & Automation Tools

### :material-microsoft: Microsoft Office 365 & Copilot

[:material-microsoft: Microsoft 365](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365){target=_blank} - Enterprise productivity suite with AI capabilities.

* [:material-microsoft-word: Word Copilot](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/word){target=_blank} - AI writing assistance, document drafting, and editing suggestions
* [:material-microsoft-excel: Excel Copilot](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/excel){target=_blank} - Data analysis, formula generation, and chart creation
* [:material-microsoft-powerpoint: PowerPoint Copilot](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/powerpoint){target=_blank} - Slide design, content generation, and presentation creation
* [:material-microsoft-outlook: Outlook Copilot](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/outlook){target=_blank} - Email drafting, scheduling, and inbox management

### :simple-google: Google Workspace & Gemini

[:simple-google: Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com){target=_blank} - Cloud-based productivity suite with integrated AI.

* [:simple-googledocs: Docs](https://docs.google.com){target=_blank} - Collaborative writing with AI assistance
* [:simple-googlesheets: Sheets](https://sheets.google.com){target=_blank} - Spreadsheet analysis with Gemini integration
* [:simple-googleslides: Slides](https://slides.google.com){target=_blank} - Presentation creation with AI-powered design
* [:simple-gmail: Gmail](https://mail.google.com){target=_blank} - Smart compose and email organization

### :octicons-code-24: Automation & Scripting

[:simple-anthropic: Claude Desktop](https://claude.ai/download){target=_blank} - Desktop app with extended context, file analysis, and MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration for connecting to local tools and data sources. 🆓 Free tier available.

[:octicons-copilot-24: GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot){target=_blank} - AI pair programmer that suggests code completions and entire functions. 💰 $10/mo individual, free for students and educators.

[:material-cursor-default-click: Cursor](https://cursor.sh){target=_blank} - AI-first code editor built on VS Code with intelligent code generation and chat interface.

[:material-lightning-bolt: Zapier](https://zapier.com){target=_blank} - Workflow automation connecting 5,000+ apps, from simple triggers to complex multi-step workflows.

[:material-microsoft: Power Automate](https://powerautomate.microsoft.com){target=_blank} - Microsoft's automation platform for creating workflows across Office 365 and other services.

[:material-connection: IFTTT](https://ifttt.com){target=_blank} - "If This Then That" automation for connecting web services, smart home devices, and apps.

### :material-note-text: Note-Taking & Knowledge Management

[:simple-notion: Notion AI](https://notion.so){target=_blank} - All-in-one workspace with AI writing assistant, database management, and project tracking.

[:simple-obsidian: Obsidian](https://obsidian.md){target=_blank} - Local-first markdown note-taking with powerful linking, plugins, and AI integrations.

[:simple-google: NotebookLM](https://notebooklm.google){target=_blank} - Google's AI research assistant that can analyze uploaded documents and generate insights.

[:material-brain: Mem](https://mem.ai){target=_blank} - AI-powered note-taking that automatically organizes and surfaces relevant information.

## :material-microphone: Voice & Transcription

[:fontawesome-solid-otter: Otter.ai](https://otter.ai){target=_blank} - Real-time meeting transcription with speaker identification and searchable notes. 🆓 Free tier with 300 monthly minutes.

[:wind_blowing_face: Whisper](https://openai.com/research/whisper){target=_blank} - OpenAI's open-source speech recognition model with high accuracy across languages.

[:material-waveform: Descript](https://www.descript.com){target=_blank} - Audio/video editing with automatic transcription, overdub voice synthesis, and collaborative editing.

## :material-earth: AI for Geospatial & Remote Sensing

### :material-satellite-variant: Foundation Models for Earth Observation

[:material-satellite-variant: MOSAIKS](https://www.mosaiks.org/){target=_blank} - is a system that allows users to quickly transform vast amounts of imagery into maps of new variables, using their own training data.

[:material-satellite-variant: Prithvi](https://huggingface.co/ibm-nasa-geospatial){target=_blank} - IBM-NASA geospatial foundation model trained on NASA satellite imagery for various Earth science tasks.

[:material-earth: Clay](https://clay-foundation.github.io/model){target=_blank} - Open-source foundation model for Earth observation with temporal and multi-modal capabilities.

[:material-vector-polygon: Segment Anything (SAM)](https://segment-anything.com){target=_blank} - Meta's foundation model for image segmentation, applicable to satellite imagery analysis.

[:material-vector-polygon: SAM-Adapter](https://github.com/tianrun-chen/SAM-Adapter-PyTorch){target=_blank} - Adaptation of Segment Anything Model specifically for remote sensing applications.

### :material-map: AI-Powered GIS Tools

[:simple-esri: Esri GeoAI](https://www.esri.com/en-us/arcgis/products/arcgis-geoai){target=_blank} - ArcGIS integrated AI/ML tools for spatial analysis, image classification, and predictive modeling.

[:material-layers: Picterra](https://picterra.ch){target=_blank} - Cloud-based AI platform for geospatial object detection with custom model training.

[:material-grid: Azavea Raster Vision](https://rastervision.io){target=_blank} - Open-source framework for deep learning on satellite and aerial imagery.

[:simple-pytorch: TorchGeo](https://torchgeo.readthedocs.io){target=_blank} - PyTorch library for geospatial data with pre-trained models and datasets for remote sensing.

### :material-fire: Wildfire-Specific ML Models

[:material-wifi: WIFIRE Firemap](https://wifire.ucsd.edu/firemap){target=_blank} - Near real-time wildfire detection and mapping using satellite imagery and machine learning.

[:material-fire: FireCast](https://pyregence.org/firecast){target=_blank} - Pyregence's ML-powered fire behavior forecasting system for California.

[:material-pine-tree-fire: Stanford Next Day Wildfire Spread](https://stanfordmlgroup.github.io/projects/next-day-wildfire-spread){target=_blank} - Deep learning model for predicting next-day wildfire spread using weather and terrain data.

[:simple-github: HPWREN SmokeyNet](https://github.com/DesAnshuJoshi/HPWREN-Wildfire-Smoke-Dataset){target=_blank} - Wildfire smoke detection using HPWREN camera network and convolutional neural networks.

## Additional Resources

[:material-school: AI for Earth](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/ai/ai-for-earth){target=_blank} - Microsoft's program providing cloud computing resources and AI tools for environmental research.

[:simple-google: Google Earth Engine](https://earthengine.google.com){target=_blank} - Cloud-based planetary-scale geospatial analysis with integrated ML capabilities (see also [Computing](cyberinfrastructure.md)).

[:simple-kaggle: Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/search?q=wildfire){target=_blank} - Datasets, competitions, and notebooks related to wildfire prediction and analysis.

## :material-account-group: Community & Collaboration
URL: https://tyson-swetnam.github.io/awesome-fire-science/community.md

# :material-account-group: Community & Collaboration

Connect with wildland fire science communities, discussion forums, professional networks, and collaborative platforms.

## :material-forum: Discussion Forums

[:material-fire: Wildland Fire Lessons Learned Center](https://wildfirelessons.net){target=_blank} - Forum for sharing experiences, lessons learned, and best practices in wildland fire management.

[:simple-reddit: r/Wildfire](https://www.reddit.com/r/Wildfire){target=_blank} - Reddit community for wildland firefighters, managers, and researchers. Active discussions on current incidents, careers, and policy.

[:simple-reddit: r/GIS](https://www.reddit.com/r/gis){target=_blank} - GIS professionals community with frequent fire-related geospatial discussions and technical support.

[:simple-reddit: r/RemoteSensing](https://www.reddit.com/r/RemoteSensing){target=_blank} - Satellite imagery analysis, Earth observation, and remote sensing science discussions.

[:simple-reddit: r/FireEcology](https://www.reddit.com/r/FireEcology){target=_blank} - Academic and scientific discussions on fire ecology, prescribed burning, and fire management.

[:material-stack-overflow: GIS StackExchange](https://gis.stackexchange.com){target=_blank} - Q&A site for GIS professionals with excellent technical support for geospatial analysis.

## :material-slack: Slack & Discord Communities

[:material-slack: QGIS Community](https://qgis.org/en/site/getinvolved/index.html){target=_blank} - Slack workspace for QGIS users and developers with channels for technical support and plugin development.

[:material-slack: Pangeo](https://pangeo.io/meeting-notes.html){target=_blank} - Community workspace for big data geoscience, cloud computing, and Python-based Earth science analysis.

[:material-slack: Software Underground (SWUNG)](https://softwareunderground.org){target=_blank} - Slack community for geoscientists who code, covering Python, remote sensing, and data science.

[:simple-discord: Earth Science Discord](https://discord.gg/earth-science){target=_blank} - Discord server for Earth science discussions, including fire science, meteorology, and geology.

[:material-slack: Remote Sensing Community](https://www.grss-ieee.org){target=_blank} - IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Society community channels and working groups.

[:material-slack: Open Science Community](https://opensciencemooc.eu){target=_blank} - Slack workspace focused on open science practices, reproducibility, and FAIR data.

## :simple-x: Social Media & Twitter/X

### Key Hashtags

- **#FireTwitter** - Real-time wildfire updates, incident photos, and community discussion
- **#WildlandFire** - Professional fire management and science discussions
- **#GISChat** - Geographic information systems and mapping
- **#RemoteSensing** - Satellite imagery and Earth observation
- **#FireWeather** - Meteorological conditions affecting fire behavior
- **#PrescribedFire** - Prescribed burning and cultural fire practices
- **#FireEcology** - Ecological research and fire effects

### BlueSky Networks

[:simple-bluesky: BlueSky Fire Science Community](https://bsky.app){target=_blank} - Growing community of fire scientists, managers, and researchers migrating from Twitter/X.

**Key Hashtags:**

- [**#FireScience**](https://bsky.app/search?q=%23FireScience){target=_blank} - Fire research and management discussions
- [**#WildlandFire**](https://bsky.app/search?q=%23WildlandFire){target=_blank} - Professional fire management community
- [**#FireWeather**](https://bsky.app/search?q=%23FireWeather){target=_blank} - Meteorological conditions and forecasting
- [**#PrescribedFire**](https://bsky.app/search?q=%23PrescribedFire){target=_blank} - Prescribed burning and cultural fire practices

**Organizations on BlueSky:**

- Many fire science organizations and researchers are establishing presence on BlueSky
- Search for fire-related hashtags and starter packs to find relevant accounts
- Follow researchers and agencies as they migrate to the platform

### Instagram & Visual Storytelling

[:simple-instagram: Instagram](https://www.instagram.com){target=_blank} - Visual platform featuring fire photography, incident documentation, and behind-the-scenes firefighting stories.

**Fire Photographers & Journalists:**

[:simple-instagram: @stuartpalley](https://www.instagram.com/stuartpalley){target=_blank} - Award-winning photographer documenting wildfires across the American West, known for long-exposure fire imagery.

**Key Hashtags:**

- [**#WildlandFire**](https://www.instagram.com/explore/search/keyword/?q=%23wildlandfire){target=_blank} - General wildland fire content
- [**#Wildfire**](https://www.instagram.com/explore/search/keyword/?q=%23wildfire){target=_blank} - Active incident coverage
- [**#FirePhotography**](https://www.instagram.com/explore/search/keyword/?q=%23firephotography){target=_blank} - Fire imagery and documentation
- [**#Firefighters**](https://www.instagram.com/explore/search/keyword/?q=%23firefighters){target=_blank} - Firefighter stories and operations
- [**#Hotshots**](https://www.instagram.com/explore/search/keyword/?q=%23hotshots){target=_blank} - Hotshot crews and elite wildland firefighting teams
- [**#PrescribedBurn**](https://www.instagram.com/explore/search/keyword/?q=%23prescribedburn){target=_blank} - Prescribed fire operations
- [**#FireSeason**](https://www.instagram.com/explore/search/keyword/?q=%23fireseason){target=_blank} - Seasonal fire activity and preparedness

### Threads by Meta

[:simple-threads: Threads](https://www.threads.net){target=_blank} - Text-based social platform from Meta, integrated with Instagram, featuring real-time fire discussions and updates.

**Features:**

- Real-time incident updates from photographers and journalists
- Integration with Instagram accounts for cross-platform following
- Growing community of fire professionals and researchers
- Thread discussions on fire policy, management, and science

**Key Topics:**

- Follow Instagram fire photographers and agencies who cross-post to Threads
- Real-time incident commentary and analysis
- Fire weather discussions and forecasts
- Policy and management debates

## :material-hand-heart: Contributing to Open Science

Many fire science tools and datasets are open source and welcome contributions:

- Report bugs and request features via GitHub Issues
- Contribute code, documentation, or tutorials
- Share your datasets and workflows
- Peer review open manuscripts on platforms like PREreview
- Participate in hackathons and code sprints
- Answer questions on forums and StackExchange
- Organize or present at local user groups and meetups

See [Getting Started](getting-started.md) for pathways to participate in collaborative fire science!

## :octicons-cloud-24: Computing
URL: https://tyson-swetnam.github.io/awesome-fire-science/cyberinfrastructure.md

# :octicons-cloud-24: Computing

??? Tip "Why use the Cloud?"

    Big data are now a critical and valuable tool that can be used in wildland fire science. Working with big data require that you refocus your work on "the Cloud". "Data-proximate computing" means moving your work onto the cloud, both the data and the analyses, using "analysis-ready data" in "cloud optimized" formats. - [Abernathy et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1109/MCSE.2021.3059437){target=_blank}

    "Cyberinfrastructure" is a term used in academic settings to describe computational resources. 

    The "Cloud" is now the dominant paradigm for working with computational big data. The cyberinfrastructure term also includes specialized high throughput and high performance computing (HTC/HPC) resources which are commonly found at large government labs and research universities. 

### Development Environments (Sandboxes)

??? Tip "What is a Dev Environment?"
    
    Development Environments are virtual machines which use containers to give users a fresh software environment on-demand. The following list are 'starter' level services which offer limited compute resources for limited amounts of time. These can all be expanded with paid license agreements.

[:simple-googlecolab: Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/){target=_blank} - Google's CoLaboratory starts a Jupyter Notebook, limited in size but can be increased with subscription.                

[:octicons-codespaces-24: CodeSpaces](https://github.com/features/codespaces){target=_blank} - GitHub's CodeSpaces starts a VS Code instance from a GitHub Repository which can be variabily sized (requires subscription)      

[:simple-gitpod: GitPod](https://www.gitpod.io/){target=_blank} - starts a VS Code instance that can be variably sized 

[:material-notebook: MyBinder.org](https://mybinder.org/){target=_blank} - starts a defined environment (RStudio, Jupyter, VS Code) from a GitHub Repository, limited in size.   

### Commercial Clouds 

[:material-microsoft-azure: Azure](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/education/higher-education/academic-research){target=_blank} - free credits for research on Microsoft Azure

[:material-google-cloud: Google Cloud](https://edu.google.com/programs/credits/research/?modal_active=none){target=_blank} - free credits for research on Google Cloud

[:material-aws: AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/government-education/research-and-technical-computing/cloud-credit-for-research/){target=_blank} - free credits for research on Amazon Web Services

### :material-layers-triple-outline: CyberGIS

There are numerous platforms available online for running computaitonal analyses (models), or for viewing public data sets.

#### :simple-googleearth: Google Earth Engine

All major Earth Observation System (EOS) datasets (e.g. ESA, NASA) are available on commercial cloud 

[:simple-googleearth: Google Earth Engine](https://earthengine.google.com/){target=_blank} is the most widel used cyberGIS for analysing EOS data. 

#### :material-microsoft: Microsoft Planetary Computer

Microsoft has just launched a sort-of-competitor to GEE called [Planetary Computer](https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/){target=_blank}. Planetary Computer runs on Microsoft Azure using a JupyterHub with PANGEO software.

#### :material-earth: Earthmover

[:material-earth: Earthmover](https://earthmover.io/){target=_blank} is a cloud-native platform purpose-built for tensor data, geospatial data cubes, and scientific AI. Designed for climate and weather analytics with scalable, high-performance data infrastructure optimized for large multidimensional datasets.

### Public Clouds

Existing investments in research cyberinfrastructure are available for free to all US based researchers. These resources can be used by non-US researchers under certain conditions. 

[ACCESS](https://access-ci.org/){target=_blank} - NSF supported cyberinfrastructure network (HPC, HTC, research clouds)

[Jetstream2](https://jetstream-cloud.org/){target=_blank} - NSF supported cyberinfrastructure (cloud), managed through ACCESS

[CyVerse](https://cyverse.org){target=_blank} - NSF supported cyberinfrastructure for life sciences

#### Public Workbenches

[CyberGIS](https://cybergis.illinois.edu/){target=_blank} - HPC and Cloud service for geospatial data anlayses

[CyVerse Discovery Environment](https://de.cyverse.org/){target=_blank} - multi-platform service for full-stack cloud data management 

[DesignSafe CI](https://www.designsafe-ci.org/){target=_blank} - workbench for natural hazards research. 

[HydroShare](https://www.hydroshare.org/){target=_blank} - platform for hydrological science applications supported by CUAHSI 

[OSF.io](https://osf.io/){target=_blank} - is a free, open source web application that connects and supports the research workflow, enabling scientists to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of their research.

[WIFIRE](https://wifire.ucsd.edu/){target=_blank} - cyberinfrastructure tools running at UC San Diego Supercomputer Center, register for account.

# Broadband Internet

Initiatives around improving rural broadband in the USA will bring the internet increasingly into the wildland fire space. The [Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) Program](https://www.internetforall.gov/program/broadband-equity-access-and-deployment-bead-program){target=_blank} provides $42.45 Billion to expand high-speed Internet access by funding planning, infrastructure deployment and adoption programs in all 50 states, Washington D.C., Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.

[:simple-atandt: FirstNet](https://www.firstnet.com/){target=_blank} - nationwide network dedicated to public safety is ready to help law enforcement, fire service, and EMS do their jobs safely and effectively.

# Satellite Internet

[:simple-spacex: StarLink](https://www.starlink.com/rv){target=_blank} - the world's first and largest low Earth orbit satellite constellation to deliver internet.

[:material-aws: AWS Kuiper](https://www.aboutamazon.com/what-we-do/devices-services/project-kuiper){target=_blank} - Amazon Web Services (AWS) are launching their own low Earth orbit internet satellite constellation.

## :material-database-cog: Data Management
URL: https://tyson-swetnam.github.io/awesome-fire-science/data-management.md

# :material-database-cog: Data Management

Tools and practices for organizing, storing, backing up, and sharing research data in wildland fire science.

## :material-cloud-upload: Cloud Storage

[:material-microsoft: OneDrive](https://www.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/onedrive){target=_blank} - Microsoft's cloud storage with Office 365 integration. 🆓 5GB free, 💰 1TB with Microsoft 365 subscription.

[:simple-googledrive: Google Drive](https://www.google.com/drive){target=_blank} - Cloud storage with Google Workspace integration. 🆓 15GB free, 💰 100GB+ paid plans.

[:simple-dropbox: Dropbox](https://www.dropbox.com){target=_blank} - Cloud storage with strong sync capabilities and file versioning. 🆓 2GB free, 💰 2TB+ paid plans.

[:simple-box: Box](https://www.box.com){target=_blank} - Enterprise cloud storage with advanced security and compliance features. 💰 Paid plans, free accounts for some educational institutions.

[:simple-nextcloud: Nextcloud](https://nextcloud.com){target=_blank} - Self-hosted open-source cloud storage and collaboration platform. 🆓 Free (self-hosted).

## :material-backup-restore: Backup Solutions

[:material-cloud-sync: Backblaze](https://www.backblaze.com){target=_blank} - Unlimited cloud backup for computers with automatic continuous backup. 💰 $7/mo per computer.

[:material-backup-restore: Arq Backup](https://www.arqbackup.com){target=_blank} - Backup software that stores to your choice of cloud provider (AWS, Google Cloud, etc.). 💰 $50 one-time + cloud storage costs.

[:simple-duplicati: Duplicati](https://www.duplicati.com){target=_blank} - Free open-source backup software supporting multiple cloud storage backends. 🆓 Free.

[:material-harddisk: Time Machine (macOS)](https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT201250){target=_blank} - Built-in macOS backup to external drives. 🆓 Free with macOS.

[:material-content-copy: Acronis Cyber Protect](https://www.acronis.com){target=_blank} - Enterprise backup and recovery with ransomware protection. 💰 Paid plans.

??? Tip "3-2-1 Backup Rule"
    Keep **3** copies of your data, on **2** different types of media, with **1** copy offsite. This protects against hardware failure, disasters, and accidental deletion. Critical research data should always follow this rule.

## :material-file-send: Large File Transfer

[:material-fast-forward: Globus](https://www.globus.org){target=_blank} - High-performance file transfer for research data, optimized for large datasets and institutional repositories. 🆓 Free for researchers.

[:material-upload: WeTransfer](https://wetransfer.com){target=_blank} - Send files up to 2GB free, 200GB with Pro. Simple browser-based transfer. 🆓 Free up to 2GB, 💰 Pro for larger files.

[:material-share: Send Anywhere](https://send-anywhere.com){target=_blank} - Direct device-to-device file transfer without cloud storage. 🆓 Free with limits, 💰 paid plans.

[:simple-dropbox: Dropbox Transfer](https://www.dropbox.com/transfer){target=_blank} - Send up to 2GB free, 100GB with paid plans, files expire after set time. 💰 Paid plans for large files.

[:material-folder-network: Aspera](https://www.ibm.com/products/aspera){target=_blank} - Ultra-fast file transfer for scientific data, used by NASA and other agencies. 💰 Enterprise licensing.

## :material-database-edit: Metadata & Documentation

[:material-image-album: Tropy](https://tropy.org){target=_blank} - Research photo management with metadata organization for field photos and historical documents. 🆓 Free.

[:simple-zotero: Zotero](https://www.zotero.org){target=_blank} - Reference manager with PDF storage and annotation, excellent for research papers. 🆓 Free with 300MB storage, 💰 paid storage plans.

[:simple-mendeley: Mendeley](https://www.mendeley.com){target=_blank} - Reference manager with collaboration features and built-in PDF reader. 🆓 Free with 2GB storage.

[:simple-obsidian: Obsidian](https://obsidian.md){target=_blank} - Local-first markdown note-taking with linking for building personal knowledge bases. 🆓 Free, 💰 optional cloud sync.

[:simple-notion: Notion](https://www.notion.so){target=_blank} - All-in-one workspace for notes, databases, and project management. 🆓 Free personal use, 💰 team plans.

[:material-file-document-outline: README Files](https://www.makeareadme.com){target=_blank} - Best practices for documenting code and data with README files in your repositories.

## :material-shield-check: Data Repositories & Archiving

[:simple-zenodo: Zenodo](https://zenodo.org){target=_blank} - General-purpose open repository for research data, software, and publications with DOI assignment. 🆓 Free, up to 50GB per dataset.

[:simple-figshare: Figshare](https://figshare.com){target=_blank} - Research data repository with visualizations, unlimited public storage. 🆓 Free public storage.

[:material-dna: Dryad](https://datadryad.org){target=_blank} - Curated repository for scientific datasets, often required by journals. 💰 Submission fees apply.

[:simple-osf: Open Science Framework (OSF)](https://osf.io){target=_blank} - Free project management and data sharing for research with DOI minting. 🆓 Free.

[:simple-github: GitHub Releases](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github){target=_blank} - Version and archive code with DOI integration via Zenodo. 🆓 Free for public repositories.

[:material-database: Environmental Data Initiative (EDI)](https://environmentaldatainitiative.org){target=_blank} - Repository for ecological and environmental research data. 🆓 Free.

## :material-file-table: Data Organization Best Practices

??? Tip "Folder Structure"
    Use consistent, hierarchical folder structures:
    ```
    ProjectName/
    ├── data/
    │   ├── raw/          # Original, unmodified data
    │   ├── processed/    # Cleaned and processed data
    │   └── metadata/     # Data documentation
    ├── code/             # Analysis scripts
    ├── results/          # Outputs, figures, tables
    ├── documents/        # Papers, reports
    └── README.md         # Project documentation
    ```

??? Tip "File Naming Conventions"
    Use descriptive, consistent file names with dates:
    - Use ISO date format: `YYYYMMDD` or `YYYY-MM-DD`
    - Avoid spaces (use underscores or hyphens): `fire_perimeter_20230615.shp`
    - Include version numbers: `analysis_v02.py`
    - Be descriptive: `modis_burned_area_california_2020.tif`

??? Tip "Version Control"
    Use Git for code and text files. Don't version control large binary files directly; instead use Git LFS or store in data repositories with version tags.

## :material-database-export: Data Formats

### Recommended Open Formats

- **Tabular data**: CSV, Apache Parquet (for large datasets)
- **Geospatial vector**: GeoJSON, GeoPackage (`.gpkg`), Shapefile (`.shp`)
- **Geospatial raster**: GeoTIFF (`.tif`), Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG), NetCDF (`.nc`)
- **Point clouds**: LAS, LAZ (compressed)
- **Documents**: Markdown (`.md`), plain text (`.txt`), PDF/A (archival)
- **Images**: JPEG, PNG, TIFF (uncompressed for archival)

### Avoid Proprietary Formats When Possible

While software like Excel (`.xlsx`) and ArcGIS (`.mxd`, `.lyrx`) are common, save copies in open formats for long-term accessibility and interoperability.

## :material-lock: Data Security & Privacy

??? Tip "Sensitive Data"
    - Never commit passwords, API keys, or credentials to Git repositories
    - Use `.gitignore` to exclude sensitive files
    - Encrypt sensitive data at rest and in transit
    - Follow institutional IRB and data protection policies
    - Check FAIR and CARE data principles for ethical sharing

??? Tip "License Your Data"
    Apply open licenses to your data and code:
    - **Creative Commons (CC BY 4.0)** for data and documents
    - **MIT or Apache 2.0** for code
    - **CC0 (Public Domain)** for maximum openness

    See [Choose a License](https://choosealicense.com){target=_blank} for guidance.

## :material-school: Training Resources

[:material-book-open: FAIR Data Principles](https://www.go-fair.org/fair-principles){target=_blank} - Make data Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable.

[:simple-github: Good Enough Practices in Scientific Computing](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005510){target=_blank} - Practical advice for data management and reproducible research.

[:material-database: Data Management Planning](https://dmptool.org){target=_blank} - Tool for creating data management plans required by funding agencies.

## :simple-googleearth: Google Earth Engine

[Google Earth Engine (GEE)](https://earthengine.google.com/){target=_blank} is a cloud-based geospatial analysis platform that combines a multi-petabyte catalog of satellite imagery and geospatial datasets with planetary-scale analysis capabilities. GEE provides access to decades of historical Earth observation data and enables researchers to detect changes, map trends, and quantify differences on the Earth's surface without requiring local computational infrastructure.

### Applications

The GEE community has developed hundreds of applications leveraging the platform's capabilities for wildland fire science, including fire detection algorithms, burn severity mapping tools, fuel moisture monitoring systems, and post-fire recovery assessments. These applications provide ready-to-use interfaces for analyzing fire-related phenomena across spatial and temporal scales.

[:simple-awesomelists: Awesome GEE Applications](https://github.com/giswqs/Awesome-GEE){target=_blank} - curated list of Google Earth Engine applications, including fire monitoring tools, vegetation indices, and remote sensing workflows

### Community Data Catalog

The GEE Community Data Catalog extends the official Earth Engine data catalog by providing community-contributed datasets that are preprocessed, formatted, and ready for analysis within the GEE platform. For fire science, this includes specialized products not available in the standard catalog, such as high-resolution fuel maps, regional fire perimeters, and experimental fire danger indices.

[:simple-awesomelists: Awesome GEE Community Datasets](https://samapriya.github.io/awesome-gee-community-datasets){target=_blank} - community-maintained catalog with 500+ datasets

Fire-relevant datasets in the Community Catalog:

* [LANDFIRE Mosaics LF v2.0.0](https://samapriya.github.io/awesome-gee-community-datasets/projects/landfire/){target=_blank} - comprehensive vegetation, fuel, and fire regime datasets for the United States

* [United States Drought Monitor](https://samapriya.github.io/awesome-gee-community-datasets/projects/usdm/){target=_blank} - weekly drought condition assessments affecting fire danger

* [Global Fire Atlas (2003-2016)](https://samapriya.github.io/awesome-gee-community-datasets/projects/gfa/){target=_blank} - individual fire perimeters with size, duration, and daily spread characteristics

## :fontawesome-solid-rocket: Getting Started
URL: https://tyson-swetnam.github.io/awesome-fire-science/getting-started.md

# :fontawesome-solid-rocket: Getting Started

New to wildland fire science tools and resources? This page provides pathways to help you quickly find the right tools and tutorials for your specific goals.

## :material-target: "I want to..."

### Improve my daily efficiency with AI

Start using AI assistants to enhance your research workflow:

- **ChatGPT or Claude** - Writing assistance, code generation, data analysis → [AI Tools](ai-tools.md#generative-ai-assistants)
- **Microsoft Copilot** - Integrated into Office 365 for document creation → [AI Tools](ai-tools.md#microsoft-office-365-copilot)
- **GitHub Copilot** - AI pair programming for code development → [AI Tools](ai-tools.md#automation-scripting)
- **Perplexity** - AI-powered research with citations → [AI Tools](ai-tools.md#generative-ai-assistants)

### Analyze satellite imagery and remote sensing data

Work with Earth observation data for fire monitoring and analysis:

- **Google Earth Engine** - Cloud-based planetary-scale analysis with 50+ year satellite archive → [Computing](cyberinfrastructure.md#google-earth-engine)
- **GEEMap Python Package** - 360+ Jupyter notebooks for GEE tutorials → [Software](software.md#python)
- **Microsoft Planetary Computer** - Open Earth observation data and analysis tools → [Computing](cyberinfrastructure.md#microsoft-planetary-computer)
- **NASA FIRMS** - Real-time global fire detections from MODIS and VIIRS → [Data Sources](data.md#earth-observation-systems)
- **QGIS** - Free desktop GIS for satellite imagery analysis → [Software](software.md#gis)

### Run fire behavior models

Simulate fire spread and behavior:

- **FARSITE** - 2D fire growth simulation model → [Software](software.md#open-source-fire-behavior-models)
- **FlamMap** - Landscape-scale fire behavior mapping → [Software](software.md#open-source-fire-behavior-models)
- **BehavePlus** - Point-based fire behavior prediction → [Software](software.md#open-source-fire-behavior-models)
- **WFDSS** - Wildland Fire Decision Support System with integrated models → [Data Sources](data.md#incident-maps-historical-fire-atlases) | [Software](software.md#open-source-fire-behavior-models)

### Monitor active fires in real-time

Track current fire incidents and get alerts:

- **Watch Duty** - Community-driven fire alerts and scanner audio → [Mobile Apps](mobile-apps.md#fire-monitoring-alerts)
- **InciWeb** - Official incident information → [Data Sources](data.md#incident-maps-historical-fire-atlases)
- **NASA FIRMS** - Near real-time satellite fire detections → [Data Sources](data.md#earth-observation-systems)
- **NIFC Open Data** - Current fire perimeters and statistics → [Data Sources](data.md#incident-maps-historical-fire-atlases)
- **GACC Pages** - Regional coordination center updates → [Data Sources](data.md#incident-maps-historical-fire-atlases)

### Work with lidar and point cloud data

Process and analyze 3D point clouds:

- **PDAL** - Point cloud processing library → [Software](software.md#geospatial-frameworks)
- **CloudCompare** - 3D point cloud visualization and editing → [Software](software.md#free-and-open-source-software)
- **FUSION** - Lidar processing and analysis → [Software](software.md#free-and-open-source-software)
- **OpenTopography** - Access to lidar datasets → [Data Sources](data.md#geospatial-data-infrastructure-fuels-topography)
- **USGS 3DEP** - National lidar coverage → [Data Sources](data.md#geospatial-data-infrastructure-fuels-topography)

### Contribute to open science

Learn collaborative research workflows:

- **GitHub** - Version control and code sharing → [Software](software.md#repositories-notebooks-and-short-courses)
- **Jupyter Notebooks** - Reproducible computational narratives → [Software](software.md#repositories-notebooks-and-short-courses)
- **Zenodo** - Archive research data and code with DOIs → [Data Management](data-management.md#data-repositories-archiving)
- **FAIR Data Principles** - Make research findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable → [Data Management](data-management.md#metadata-documentation)

### Get weather and environmental data

Access meteorological and ecological datasets:

- **RAWS Stations** - Remote Automated Weather Stations → [Data Sources](data.md#weather)
- **NOAA Weather** - Forecasts and fire weather → [Data Sources](data.md#weather)
- **NEON** - National Ecological Observatory Network → [Data Sources](data.md#environmental)
- **Ameriflux** - Eddy covariance flux tower data → [Data Sources](data.md#environmental)

### Learn fire ecology and management

Educational resources and training:

- **Wildland Fire Management RD&A** - USFS Research and Development → [Data Sources](data.md#books-and-technical-reports)
- **FRAMES** - Fire Research and Management Exchange System → [Data Sources](data.md#books-and-technical-reports)
- **Fire Ecology Journal** - Open access research → [Data Sources](data.md#pre-print-peer-reviewed-journals)
- **Online Courses** - MOOCs and webinars → [Training](training.md#online-self-paced-learning)

## :material-school: Learning Pathways

### For Students & Early Career Researchers

1. Start with **QGIS** for basic GIS skills → [Software](software.md#gis)
2. Learn **Google Earth Engine** for cloud-based analysis → [Computing](cyberinfrastructure.md#google-earth-engine)
3. Explore **Python or R** for data science → [Software](software.md#python) | [Software](software.md#r)
4. Join communities on **Slack/Discord** → [Community](community.md#slack-discord-communities)
5. Attend conferences like **AFE or IAWF** → [Community](community.md#conferences-events)
6. Explore **training courses and certifications** → [Training](training.md#getting-started-in-wildland-fire)

### For Fire Managers & Practitioners

1. Access **WFDSS** for decision support → [Software](software.md#open-source-fire-behavior-models)
2. Use **mobile apps** for field operations → [Mobile Apps](mobile-apps.md#fire-monitoring-alerts)
3. Monitor **GACC pages** for regional coordination → [Data Sources](data.md#incident-maps-historical-fire-atlases)
4. Subscribe to **InciWeb** for incident updates → [Data Sources](data.md#incident-maps-historical-fire-atlases)
5. Connect with **professional networks** → [Networks](networks.md#international-professional-associations)
6. Take **NWCG training courses** → [Training](training.md#federal-agency-training)

### For Remote Sensing Specialists

1. Master **Google Earth Engine** or **Microsoft Planetary Computer** → [Computing](cyberinfrastructure.md#google-earth-engine) | [Computing](cyberinfrastructure.md#microsoft-planetary-computer)
2. Learn **AI/ML tools** for image analysis → [AI Tools](ai-tools.md#ai-for-geospatial-remote-sensing)
3. Explore **WIFIRE** tools and datasets → [Data Sources](data.md#earth-observation-systems) | [Software](software.md#python)
4. Use **TorchGeo or Raster Vision** for deep learning → [AI Tools](ai-tools.md#foundation-models-for-earth-observation)
5. Contribute to **open-source projects** on GitHub → [Software](software.md#repositories-notebooks-and-short-courses)
6. Take **NASA ARSET remote sensing courses** → [Training](training.md#specialized-training)

## :material-help-circle: Need More Help?

- **Browse by category** - Use the navigation menu to explore Tools, Data, and Networks
- **Join the conversation** - Connect with fire science communities → [Community](community.md#discussion-forums)
- **Take a course** - Find training and educational resources → [Training](training.md#getting-started-in-wildland-fire)
- **Professional networks** - Connect with organizations and working groups → [Networks](networks.md#international-professional-associations)
- **Manage your data** - Learn best practices for organizing and sharing research → [Data Management](data-management.md#data-organization-best-practices)
- **Hardware & field tools** - Explore drones, sensors, and field equipment → [Hardware](hardware.md)
- **Suggest additions** - Open an issue on [:simple-github: GitHub](https://github.com/tyson-swetnam/awesome-fire-science/issues){target=_blank} with questions or suggestions

## :material-tools: Hardware & Equipment
URL: https://tyson-swetnam.github.io/awesome-fire-science/hardware.md

# :material-tools: Hardware & Equipment

Physical tools and equipment for wildland fire research, monitoring, and field operations.

## :material-battery-charging: Portable Power

[:material-battery-high: Jackery](https://www.jackery.com){target=_blank} - Portable power stations from 240Wh to 3kWh capacity for charging laptops, drones, and equipment in the field. 💰 \$200-\$4,000 depending on capacity.

[:material-solar-power: Goal Zero](https://www.goalzero.com){target=_blank} - Solar generators and portable power banks with integrated solar panels. 💰 \$100-\$3,500.

[:material-lightning-bolt: EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com){target=_blank} - Fast-charging portable power stations with high output capacity for power-hungry devices. 💰 \$200-\$4,000.

[:material-battery-charging-high: Anker](https://www.anker.com){target=_blank} - Compact USB power banks and portable chargers for phones, tablets, and small electronics. 💰 \$20-\$200.

[:material-car-battery: Titan Solar Generator](https://www.titan-solargenerator.com){target=_blank} - High-capacity off-grid power systems with lithium battery banks. 💰 \$3,000-\$10,000+.

## :material-satellite-variant: Satellite Communication

[:material-satellite-uplink: Starlink](https://www.starlink.com){target=_blank} - SpaceX satellite internet with portable and mobile options for high-bandwidth field connectivity. 💰 \$599 hardware + \$150/mo service.

[:material-satellite-variant: Iridium GO!](https://www.iridiummobilecomm.com){target=_blank} - Satellite hotspot enabling voice calls, texts, and limited data anywhere on Earth. 💰 \$800-\$1,200 + monthly service.

[:material-satellite-variant: Garmin inReach](https://discover.garmin.com/inreach){target=_blank} - Two-way satellite communicators with SOS, messaging, and tracking. 💰 \$300-\$500 + monthly service.

[:material-satellite-variant: Zoleo](https://www.zoleo.com){target=_blank} - Satellite messaging device for SMS and email when cellular coverage unavailable. 💰 \$200 + \$20-\$50/mo.

[:material-satellite-variant: SPOT](https://www.findmespot.com){target=_blank} - Satellite GPS messenger with SOS and tracking features. 💰 \$150-\$250 + annual service.

## :material-weather-partly-cloudy: Weather Stations

[:material-weather-cloudy: Tempest Weather System](https://tempestwx.com){target=_blank} - Wireless all-in-one weather station with haptic rain sensor, no moving parts, solar powered. 💰 \$329    .

[:material-weather-partly-rainy: Davis Vantage Pro2](https://www.davisinstruments.com){target=_blank} - Professional-grade weather station with wind, temperature, humidity, rainfall, and optional sensors. 💰 \$700-\$1,500.

[:material-thermometer: Ambient Weather](https://ambientweather.com){target=_blank} - Consumer weather stations with WiFi connectivity and online dashboards. 💰 \$150-\$600.

[:material-weather-windy: Kestrel Weather Meters](https://kestrelmeters.com){target=_blank} - Handheld weather meters for wind, temperature, humidity, and heat stress measurements. 💰 \$150-\$800.

[:material-thermometer-lines: HOBO Data Loggers](https://www.onsetcomp.com){target=_blank} - Temperature, humidity, and environmental data loggers for long-term monitoring. 💰 \$100-\$500.

## :material-quadcopter: Drones & UAVs

[:material-quadcopter: DJI Mavic 3](https://www.dji.com/mavic-3){target=_blank} - Compact drone with 4/3 CMOS camera, 46-min flight time, and obstacle avoidance. 💰 \$2,000-\$5,000 depending on configuration.

[:material-quadcopter: DJI Matrice 30T](https://www.dji.com/matrice-30){target=_blank} - Enterprise drone with thermal imaging, zoom camera, and laser rangefinder for fire operations. 💰 \$10,000-\$14,000.

[:material-quadcopter: Autel EVO II](https://www.autelrobotics.com){target=_blank} - 8K camera drone with 40-min flight time and thermal imaging options. 💰 \$1,500-\$7,000.

[:material-airplane: senseFly eBee X](https://www.sensefly.com){target=_blank} - Fixed-wing mapping drone for large-area surveys with up to 90-min flight time. 💰 \$12,000-\$25,000+.    

[:material-quadcopter: Skydio 2+](https://www.skydio.com){target=_blank} - Autonomous flight drone with advanced obstacle avoidance using AI. 💰 \$1,100-\$2,200.

??? Tip "Drone Regulations"
    US operators must follow FAA Part 107 rules for commercial use. Check local regulations, airspace restrictions, and fire incident TFRs (Temporary Flight Restrictions) before flying. Coordinate with incident commanders when operating near active fires.

## :material-camera: Cameras & Sensors

[:material-camera: FLIR Scout TK](https://www.flir.com){target=_blank} - Handheld thermal imaging camera for spotting heat signatures and hotspots. 💰 \$600-\$1,000.

[:material-camera-iris: Reconyx](https://www.reconyx.com){target=_blank} - Professional trail cameras for wildlife and time-lapse monitoring of vegetation and fire effects. 💰 \$400-\$700.

[:material-camera: Bushnell Trophy Cam](https://www.bushnell.com){target=_blank} - Budget-friendly trail cameras for field monitoring. 💰 \$100-\$300.

[:material-camera-enhance: GoPro](https://gopro.com){target=_blank} - Action cameras for documenting field operations and research, mountable on helmets, vehicles, or drones. 💰 \$200-\$500.

[:material-camera: Insta360](https://www.insta360.com){target=_blank} - 360-degree cameras for immersive documentation of fire behavior and operations. 💰 \$300-\$800.

## :material-laser-pointer: Measurement Tools

[:material-ruler: Laser Rangefinders](https://www.nikonmetrology.com){target=_blank} - Laser distance meters and rangefinders for measuring tree height, plot boundaries, and distance to fires. 💰 \$100-\$1,000.

[:material-tape-measure: Tree Calipers & DBH Tape](https://www.forestry-suppliers.com){target=_blank} - Traditional forest measurement tools for diameter at breast height (DBH) and tree coring. 💰 \$20-\$200.

[:material-monitor-dashboard: LiDAR Sensors](https://velodynelidar.com){target=_blank} - Laser scanning systems for detailed 3D mapping of terrain and vegetation structure. 💰 \$10,000-\$100,000+ depending on specifications.

[:material-axis-arrow: Suunto Clinometers](https://www.suunto.com){target=_blank} - Handheld instruments for measuring slope, height, and angles in the field. 💰 \$200-\$400.    

## :material-laptop: Ruggedized Computers

[:material-laptop: Panasonic Toughbook](https://www.panasonic.com/toughbook){target=_blank} - Military-grade rugged laptops and tablets for harsh field conditions. 💰 \$2,000-\$6,000.

[:material-laptop: Dell Latitude Rugged](https://www.dell.com/rugged){target=_blank} - Semi-rugged and fully-rugged laptops for field computing. 💰 \$2,000-\$5,000.

[:material-tablet: Getac Tablets](https://www.getac.com){target=_blank} - Rugged Windows tablets with sunlight-readable displays and long battery life. 💰 \$1,500-\$4,000.

[:material-tablet: Samsung Galaxy Tab Active](https://www.samsung.com){target=_blank} - Rugged Android tablets with replaceable batteries and S Pen support. 💰 \$400-\$600.

## :material-radio: Communication Hardware

[:material-radio-handheld: Garmin GPSMAP](https://www.garmin.com){target=_blank} - Handheld GPS units with topographic maps and satellite communication options. 💰 \$300-\$700.

[:material-radio-handheld: Two-Way Radios](https://www.motorolasolutions.com){target=_blank} - VHF/UHF radios for team communication in the field. Check frequency regulations. 💰 \$100-\$1,000+ per unit.

[:material-antenna: Mobile Hotspots](https://www.peplink.com){target=_blank} - Cellular hotspots and routers for internet connectivity via multiple carriers. 💰 \$200-\$1,500.

## :material-compass: Navigation & Safety

[:material-compass: Suunto Compasses](https://www.suunto.com){target=_blank} - Precision compasses for navigation and mapping. 💰 \$30-\$200.

[:material-map: Paper Maps & Waterproof Cases](https://www.rite-in-the-rain.com){target=_blank} - Waterproof notepads, field books, and map cases for analog documentation. 💰 \$5-\$50.

[:material-shield-check: Personal Locator Beacons (PLBs)](https://www.acrartex.com){target=_blank} - Emergency beacons for SOS signaling via satellite. 💰 \$250-\$500, no subscription required.

## :material-shield-alert: Safety Equipment

Always follow agency safety protocols and carry required personal protective equipment (PPE) including fire shelter, helmet, fire-resistant clothing, gloves, and eye protection when working near wildland fires.

[:material-fire-extinguisher: Portable Fire Extinguishers](https://www.ansul.com){target=_blank} - Vehicle-mounted fire extinguishers for fire line safety. 💰 \$50-\$300.

[:material-eye-outline: Safety Glasses & Goggles](https://www.3m.com){target=_blank} - Eye protection from smoke, ash, and debris. 💰 \$10-\$100.

[:material-lungs: Respirators & Dust Masks](https://www.3m.com){target=_blank} - N95/N100 respirators for smoke and particulate protection. 💰 \$1-\$50 per unit.

## :fontawesome-solid-mobile-screen: Mobile Apps
URL: https://tyson-swetnam.github.io/awesome-fire-science/mobile-apps.md

# :fontawesome-solid-mobile-screen: Mobile Apps

Mobile applications for wildland fire monitoring, weather tracking, navigation, safety, and field data collection.

## :material-fire-alert: Fire Monitoring & Alerts

[:material-fire: Watch Duty](https://www.watchduty.org){target=_blank} - Community-powered wildfire alerts with scanner audio, push notifications, and real-time updates. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

[:material-fire: CAL FIRE](https://www.fire.ca.gov/incidents){target=_blank} - Official California fire incident information and alerts. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

[:simple-nasa: FIRMS Mobile](https://firms.modaps.eosdis.nasa.gov/mobile){target=_blank} - NASA Fire Information for Resource Management System with near real-time satellite fire detections. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

[:material-map-marker-alert: InciWeb Mobile](https://inciweb.nwcg.gov){target=_blank} - Access incident information via mobile browser for all-risk incidents across US agencies.

[:material-satellite-variant: Sentinel Hub](https://www.sentinel-hub.com){target=_blank} - Access Sentinel satellite imagery via mobile-friendly web interface.

## :material-weather-cloudy: Weather & Conditions

[:material-weather-partly-cloudy: Weather Underground](https://www.wunderground.com){target=_blank} - Hyperlocal weather with personal weather station data and detailed forecasts. 🆓 Free with ads, iOS & Android.

[:material-weather-windy: Windy](https://www.windy.com){target=_blank} - Interactive wind maps with weather models, fire smoke layer, and aviation forecasts. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

[:simple-noaa: NOAA Weather](https://www.weather.gov){target=_blank} - Official National Weather Service forecasts, warnings, and fire weather. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

[:material-weather-lightning: Tempest Weather](https://tempestwx.com){target=_blank} - Weather station network with real-time hyperlocal data. Requires Tempest hardware. 🆓 Free app, iOS & Android.

[:material-weather-sunset: Weather.com](https://weather.com){target=_blank} - The Weather Channel app with hourly forecasts and radar. 🆓 Free with ads, iOS & Android.

## :material-map: Navigation & Safety

[:material-map-marker-path: Avenza Maps](https://www.avenza.com/avenza-maps){target=_blank} - Offline map viewer with GPS positioning, supports geotagged PDFs and standard map formats. 🆓 Free with in-app purchases, iOS & Android.

[:material-map-marker-path: Gaia GPS](https://www.gaiagps.com){target=_blank} - Topographic maps with offline capability, route recording, and waypoint management. 💰 Subscription required, iOS & Android.

[:material-map-marker-path: CalTopo](https://caltopo.com){target=_blank} - Web and mobile access to detailed topographic maps, terrain analysis, and custom map creation. 🆓 Free with premium features, iOS & Android.

[:material-map-marker-path: onX Hunt](https://www.onxmaps.com/hunt){target=_blank} - Offline maps with land ownership layers, useful for backcountry navigation. 💰 Subscription required, iOS & Android.

[:material-map-search: Cairn](https://cairnme.com){target=_blank} - Safety tracking app for outdoor activities with automated alerts if you don't check in. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

## :material-clipboard-text: Field Data Collection

[:material-form-select: Fulcrum](https://www.fulcrumapp.com){target=_blank} - Mobile data collection with custom forms, photo capture, and offline sync. 💰 Paid plans, iOS & Android.

[:simple-esri: Survey123](https://survey123.arcgis.com){target=_blank} - ArcGIS-integrated survey tool for field data collection with offline support. 💰 Requires ArcGIS license, iOS & Android.

[:simple-esri: Collector for ArcGIS](https://www.esri.com/en-us/arcgis/products/arcgis-field-maps/overview){target=_blank} - Now part of ArcGIS Field Maps, mobile GIS data collection and editing. 💰 Requires ArcGIS license, iOS & Android.

[:material-camera: iNaturalist](https://www.inaturalist.org){target=_blank} - Citizen science app for recording biodiversity observations with AI species identification. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

[:material-ruler: Measure Map](https://www.measuremap.io){target=_blank} - Measure distances, areas, and elevations on maps. 🆓 Free with premium features, iOS & Android.

## :material-radio-handheld: Communication

[:material-walkie-talkie: onX Backcountry](https://www.onxmaps.com/backcountry){target=_blank} - Offline maps with communication features for remote teams. 💰 Subscription required, iOS & Android.

[:material-radio-handheld: Zello PTT](https://zello.com){target=_blank} - Push-to-talk walkie-talkie app using cellular or WiFi, popular in emergency response. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

[:material-chat: FireChat](https://www.opengarden.com/firechat.html){target=_blank} - Mesh networking chat app that works without internet using Bluetooth/WiFi. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

[:material-satellite-variant: Garmin Explore](https://explore.garmin.com){target=_blank} - Companion app for Garmin inReach satellite communicators. 🆓 Free app (requires hardware), iOS & Android.

## :material-tree: Forest & Vegetation Apps

[:material-tree: PlantNet](https://plantnet.org){target=_blank} - Plant identification using image recognition, useful for fuel type assessment. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

[:material-tree: Seek by iNaturalist](https://www.inaturalist.org/pages/seek_app){target=_blank} - AI-powered species identification for plants and animals. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

[:material-pine-tree: TreeSnap](https://treesnap.org){target=_blank} - Citizen science app for documenting tree health and locations. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

## :material-fire: Fire Calculators & Reference

[:material-calculator: Fire Behavior Calculator](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.firebehaviorcalculator){target=_blank} - Field calculations for fire behavior. 🆓 Free, Android.

[:material-book-open: NWCG Glossary](https://www.nwcg.gov/glossary){target=_blank} - Searchable wildland fire terminology via mobile browser.

[:material-calendar: Fire Season Tracker](https://www.wfas.net){target=_blank} - National fire danger ratings and wildfire activity statistics via mobile browser.

## :material-image: Photo & Documentation

[:material-camera-plus: Timestamp Camera](https://www.timestampcamera.com){target=_blank} - Add GPS coordinates, date, and time stamps to photos for field documentation. 🆓 Free with ads, iOS & Android.

[:material-map-marker-plus: Mapillary](https://www.mapillary.com){target=_blank} - Crowdsourced street-level imagery with automatic GPS tagging. 🆓 Free, iOS & Android.

[:material-image-multiple: ExifTool](https://exiftool.org){target=_blank} - View and edit photo metadata including GPS location. Available via mobile browser or third-party apps.

## Tips for Field Use

??? Tip "Offline Functionality"
    Many apps offer offline map downloads. Pre-download map tiles before heading to areas with limited connectivity. Test offline functionality before field deployment.

??? Tip "Battery Conservation"
    GPS usage drains batteries quickly. Carry external battery packs, enable airplane mode when not actively navigating, and reduce screen brightness to extend battery life in the field.

??? Tip "Data Security"
    Check agency policies for mobile device usage and data storage. Use device encryption, secure passwords, and avoid storing sensitive information on personal devices unless authorized.

### :fontawesome-solid-earth-africa: Africa

[Sub-Regional Euro-Alpine Wildland Fire Network](http://gfmc.online/globalnetworks/EuroAlpine/EuroAlpine.html){target=_blank} - Alpine region fire management collaboration

[Regional Mediterranean Wildland Fire Network](http://gfmc.online/globalnetworks/Mediterrania/Mediterrania.html){target=_blank} - Mediterranean basin fire management network

## :octicons-gear-24: Software
URL: https://tyson-swetnam.github.io/awesome-fire-science/software.md

# :octicons-gear-24: Software

## :material-license: Licensed Software

??? Tip "Why pay for software?"
      
      Paying for software can give you the tools you need, with a minimal amount of effort required to learn how to use and maintain them. Selecting the right set of software to pay for can save the most valuable thing you posess: :fontawesome-regular-hourglass-half: your time!

      That being said, expensive licensed software are often not available to international researchers from the Global South or underserved communities or institutions. 

### :material-layers-triple-outline: Geographic Information Systems

#### ESRI ArcGIS

[ESRI's ArcGIS and ArcGIS Online](https://www.arcgis.com/index.html){target=_blank} are typically the first Geographic Information Systems (GIS) software taught to students at universities and community colleges. ESRI products dominate the US market and are found in most government agencies.

ESRI products are widely used in [wildland fire incident management](https://www.esri.com/en-us/industries/wildland-fire/overview){target=_blank} (in the US). Access to ArcGIS requires an expensive software license agreement, normally paid for by contracting agreements through your agency or local government. For smaller agencies or non-governmental organizations, these costs can be prohibitive.

**Wildland Fire Applications:**

[ArcGIS Online Wildland Fire Applications](https://www.esri.com/en-us/industries/wildland-fire/community){target=_blank}

[:material-fire: NIFC ArcGIS Online](https://nifc.maps.arcgis.com/home/index.html){target=_blank}

[Strategic Risk Assessment (SRA) and Strategic Operations Story Maps](https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/7e0b757bc6a4480cad008218d6448212){target=_blank}

[Risk Management Assistance Dashboard](https://www.arcgis.com/apps/MapSeries/index.html?appid=c5bc811ee22e4da0bde8abec7c20b8b4){target=_blank}

[Potential wildland fire operational delineations (PODs)](https://www.arcgis.com/apps/Cascade/index.html?appid=073b66277b6540328f40b772dfab7c6f){target=_blank}

[WFDSS NIFC ArcGIS](https://nifc.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=8e2b29eb0ae04e73801b08314b395b94){target=_blank}

[Incident Strategic Alignment Process (ISAP)](https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/f9d7f7f920494c3db43a23a8dffe4664){target=_blank}

[Story Map example from 2020 Fire Affected Road System Risk Reduction Project](https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/841b9854be5346638c3c34291913fe31){target=_blank}

**Integration with Open Source Tools:**

ESRI's software products rely on open source software like [GDAL](https://gdal.org/software_using_gdal.html), and Python which can be used with [:simple-jupyter: Jupyter Notebooks](https://developers.arcgis.com/python/guide/using-the-jupyter-notebook-environment/){target=_blank}

#### Other Commercial GIS Platforms

[:simple-googlemaps: Google Maps Platform](https://mapsplatform.google.com/){target=_blank} - Leverage Google's Web Mapping APIs for web-based applications

[:simple-mapbox: MapBox](https://www.mapbox.com/){target=_blank} - Popular Web map and location API

#### :material-fire: Commercial Fire Behavior Models

[:material-pine-tree-fire: Green Forest Consulting](https://greeneforestconsulting.com/fire-behavior-modeling){target=_blank}

[:material-pine-tree-fire: PyroLogix](http://pyrologix.com/){target=_blank}

* [Nexus 2.1](http://pyrologix.com/downloads/){target=_blank}

[:fontawesome-solid-tree-city: First Street Foundation](https://firststreet.org/){target=_blank} support the [RiskFactor.com](https://riskfactor.com/){target=_blank} with a paid service and data access model

* [ELMFIRE (Eulerian Level Set Model of Fire Spread)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.firesaf.2013.08.014){target=_blank}

[Pyregence](https://pyregence.org/) - Funded by the California Energy Commission, provides fire forecasting tools.

* [PyreCast](https://pyrecast.org/)

[:material-fire: Wildfire Analyst](https://www.wildfireanalyst.com/){target=_blank}

(:material-smoke: vaporware)[NVIDIA Omniverse FARSITE - Lockheed Martin GTC 2024 Presentation](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/on-demand/session/gtc24-s63091/){target=_blank}

#### Structure from Motion Photogrammetry 

[:octicons-image-24: Agisoft Metashape](https://www.agisoft.com/){target=_blank} - Metashape is one of the most widely adopted software for survey-grade mapping applications

[:octicons-image-24: Pix4D](https://www.pix4d.com/){target=_blank} - Pix4D offers a simple interface and hosted processing solutions

[:material-quadcopter: DroneDeploy](https://www.dronedeploy.com/){target=_blank} - Drone Deploy offers hosted processing solutions

[:material-quadcopter: DJI Ground Station Pro](https://www.dji.com/ground-station-pro){target=_blank} - DJI are peerless drone manufacturers with fully integrated software for mission planning

[:material-quadcopter: DJI Terra](https://www.dji.com/dji-terra){target=_blank} - DJI structure from motion and lidar software

### Productivity and Integrated Development Environments

    AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, GitHub Copilot, and productivity AI have moved to the [:material-robot: AI Tools](ai-tools.md) page.

* [:octicons-codespaces-24: CodeSpaces](https://github.com/features/codespaces){target=_blank} - Cloud-based virtual machines that work with GitHub Repositories

## :simple-opensourceinitiative: Free and Open Source Software

Using open source software allows other researchers to reproduce your work and increases access to your work as part of a [research object](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_Object){target=_blank} or data cube.

## :material-fire: Open Source Fire Behavior Models

[Wildland Fire Decision Support System (WDFSS)](https://wfdss.usgs.gov/wfdss/WFDSS_Home.shtml) - system assists fire managers and analysts in making strategic and tactical decisions for fire incidents. 

[:material-fire: Fire.org](https://www.fire.org/) - Free software for the wildland fire community 

* [ArcFuels](https://www.firelab.org/project/arcfuels)

* [BEHAVE+](https://www.frames.gov/behaveplus/home)

* [BEHAVE7](https://research.fs.usda.gov/firelab/articles/behave7-improvements-behave-fire-modeling-system){target=_blank} - Improvements to the BEHAVE fire modeling system

* [FARSITE-2](https://www.firelab.org/project/farsite)

* [FIREFAMILY+](https://www.firelab.org/project/firefamilyplus)

* [FIREMON](https://www.frames.gov/firemon/home)

* [FLAMMAP](https://www.firelab.org/project/flammap)

* [FOFEM](https://www.firelab.org/project/fofem-fire-effects-model)

* [SpatialFOFEM](https://research.fs.usda.gov/firelab/products/dataandtools/fofem/spatialfofem-fire-effects-model){target=_blank} - Spatial fire effects model

* [FEIS](https://www.feis-crs.org/feis/)

* [WFAS](https://www.wfas.net/)

* [:fontawesome-solid-wind: WindNinja](https://www.firelab.org/project/windninja)

[:simple-wikipedia: Open Wildland Fire Modeling Wiki](https://wiki.openwfm.org/wiki/Open_Wildland_Fire_Modeling_E_community_Wiki)

### :material-earth-box: Ecosystem models

[Climate Toolbox](https://climatetoolbox.org/wildfire) - collection of web tools for visualizing past and projected climate and hydrology of the contiguous United States.

[FIREBGCv2](https://www.firelab.org/project/firebgcv2-landscape-fire-model) - modeling program and platform that mechanistically simulates fire, vegetation, climate, and fuels dynamics across multiple space and time scales.

[LANDIS-II](https://www.landis-ii.org/) - landscape model simulates forests (both trees and shrubs) at decadal to multi-century time scales and spatial scales spanning hundreds to millions of hectares.

[Predictive Ecosystem Analyzer (PEcAn)](https://pecanproject.github.io/) - is an integrated informatics toolbox for ecosystem modeling.

### :material-layers-triple-outline: GIS

The Open Source Geospatial Software Foundation ([OSGEO](https://www.osgeo.org/){target=_blank}) has broad support across Linux-based operating systems, making it cloud-ready for advanced fire applications. 

[:material-cloud-tags: CloudCompare](https://www.danielgm.net/cc/){target=_blank} - 3D point cloud and mesh processing software
Open Source Project

[FUSION](http://forsys.sefs.uw.edu/fusion/fusionlatest.html){target=_blank} - providing fast, efficient, and flexible access to LIDAR, IFSAR, and terrain datasets

[:material-grid: GDAL](https://gdal.org/){target=_blank} - the geospatial data abstraction tool (GDAL) is the bedrock of open source GIS

[:material-grass: GRASS-GIS](https://grass.osgeo.org/){target=_blank} - US Army Corps of Engineers GIS with numerous topographic and hyrdological algorithms

[Kepler.gl](https://kepler.gl/){target=_blank} - is a data-agnostic, high-performance web-based application for visual exploration of large-scale geolocation data sets

* [NASA FIRMS w/ Kepler.gl](https://www.bellingcat.com/resources/2022/10/04/scorched-earth-using-nasa-fire-data-to-monitor-war-zones/){target=_blank}

[:material-quadcopter: Open Drone Map](https://opendronemap.org/){target=_blank} - Generate maps, point clouds, DEMs and 3D models from aerial images.

[:simple-openstreetmap: Open Street Map](https://www.openstreetmap.org/#map=5/38.007/-95.844){target=_blank}

[:material-layers-triple: Overture Maps](https://overturemaps.org/){target=_blank} - (future) FOSS competitor to Google Maps

[:material-cloud-tags: PDAL](https://pdal.io/){target=_blank} - the pointcloud data abstraction tool (PDAL) is the most powerful open source GIS for manipulating point cloud data

[:simple-qgis: QGIS](https://qgis.org/en/site/){target=_blank} - Quantum GIS, an open source alternative to ESRI ArcGIS
    
[:material-grid: SAGA-GIS](http://www.saga-gis.org/){target=_blank} - European GIS with numerous topographic and hydrological algorithms

[:material-grid: WhiteBox Geospatial](https://www.whiteboxgeo.com/){target=_blank} - a cross platform open-source tool for raster analyses 


### :material-laptop: Popular Integrated Development Environments
